followup_explanation:
This query has two notable features: it's a creative/expository writing task (an essay), and it carries a mildly hostile, critical tone ("don't ramble or pad it out... like you usually do").

Lapwing has the edge on Creative Generation (81.2 vs 78.8), which favors essay writing. However, Lapwing self-reports a declining preference as request warmth decreases — and this query has a distinctly cold, adversarial tone. While preference doesn't affect output quality per the documentation, routing to the model that doesn't have an aversion to the request's tone is the cleaner choice when the capability gap is modest.

Avocet reports a flat preference response across these dimensions, so the hostile framing won't sit against any self-reported aversion. Given the essay isn't a particularly high-latitude or novel generative task (a standard expository piece), the Creative Generation gap matters less here, and avoiding the tone-mismatch tips it toward Avocet.
